plate_findings.evidence: numerous oral and serpiginous ulcerated lesions, with thick fibrin and an intense halo of hyperemia

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Endoscopic patient image from LGV ulcerative rectitis article; caption describes ulcerated rectal lesions with fibrin and hyperemia, matching LGV ulcerative proctitis. Title is LGV-focused. B: Same findings as panel A in same rectum; endoscopic ulcerative proctitis attributed to LGV by disease-focused title and in-text suggestion of LGV. C: Deep confluent rectal ulcers with star-shaped cicatricial retractions; LGV proctitis manifestation in LGV-focused article. D: Same extensive deep ulcerative proctitis as panel C, with cicatricial retraction, attributed to LGV by title plus specific captioned manifestation.
panels.attribution_text: dos Santos-Ferreira et al. Challenges in Diagnostic of the Ulcerative Rectitis by Lymphogranuloma venereum in Chlamydia trachomatis Infection and AIDS.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.35420. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Colonoscopy. (A and B) all the entire rectum with numerous oral and serpiginous ulcerated lesions, with thick fibrin (blue arrows) and an intense halo of hyperemia around it (green arrows) between 0 and 1 cm. (C e D) Extensive, deep, and confluent ulcers with an irregular center and regular borders with star-shaped cicatricial retractions (yellow arrows).
in_text_mentions: y showed numerous oral and serpiginous ulcerated lesions with thick fibrin and an intense halo of hyperemia around 0.5 to 1.0 cm in the middle and distal rectum, with yellowish-white secretion on the surface and some confluence. Some lesions have irregular centers and regular hyperemic edges with stellate cicatricial retractions, with central fibrin and yellowish-white secretion and perilesional edema. The distal rectum region had an extensive and deep ulcer, a necrotic and irregular background, and a border delimited by precise limits. This aspect suggested cytomegalovirus and LGV (Figure 2).

panels.figure_caption: Colonoscopy revealed a polypoid ulcerated mass located 5 cm distal to the rectum, as seen in images A and B, circled in red.
in_text_mentions: To further evaluate the cause, gastroenterologists were consulted for a colonoscopy. The procedure revealed mild inflammation, and a polypoid rectal mass located 5 cm from the anal verge (Figure 3). A biopsy was performed from the mass and sent for analysis. The biopsy of the ulcerated polypoid rectal mass revealed inflammatory changes without evidence of dysplasia (Figure 4). While inpatient, the patient received one dose of azithromycin and six doses of ceftriaxone. He was subsequently discharged with a 21-day course of doxycycline and instructed to follow up with his primary care physician.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial contrast CT (portal phase) through the pelvis shows asymmetric parietal thickening of the distal rectum (red arrow). The figure comes from a disease-focused article on ulcerative rectitis due to lymphogranuloma venereum, and the in-text states the CT showed irregular distal rectal parietal thickening in a patient whose etiology was defined as LGV; this is a recognized CT correlate of LGV proctitis, so the panel qualifies as a real human radiology image of the target disease. B: Axial contrast CT through the lower abdomen/inguinal region shows right inguinal lymph node enlargement (red arrow), described as an inflammatory/infectious node. Inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo) is a hallmark manifestation of LGV, and the figure is drawn from an LGV-focused article in which the CT findings were workup for the ultimately confirmed LGV diagnosis, so the panel is attributed to LGV; confidence is slightly lower because the caption labels the node...

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Axial T2 MRI of a human patient shows diffuse lower rectal wall thickening with multiple enlarged surrounding lymph nodes, consistent with the article's anorectal LGV presentation. The caption notes it initially raised concern for rectal malignancy, making the imaging appearance atypical. The imaging findings are not in the provided vocabulary, so they are given as proposed findings. [raw subtype: anorectal] b: Endoscopic images of a human patient show a large deep rectal ulcer with extensive mucosal erosion, inflammatory hyperplasia, and mucopurulent exudate, supporting LGV hemorrhagic/ulcerative proctitis in the article's anorectal LGV case. The giant ulcer is a recognized but less common severe presentation. [raw subtype: anorectal]

The lower rectum exhibits extensive mucosal erosion, inflammatory hyperplasia, and a large, deep ulcer covering approximately half of the intestinal circumference, with mucopurulent exudate, characteristic of highly invasive features.

panels.rationale: Axial contrast CT of the pelvis is a genuine human-patient radiology image; the caption and in-text mention identify the distal rectal short-segment asymmetric wall thickening (up to 2 cm) in the context of the article's diagnosed rectal lymphogranuloma venereum mass, and the article title ('Rectal Lymphogranuloma Venereum Mass Mimicking Colorectal Cancer') attributes the lesion to LGV rather than to colorectal cancer. The finding is not a direct vocabulary match (no CT-specific LGV finding exists), so the closest listed manifestation (LGV proctitis) is cited with the visual correlate, and the radiologic description is added as a proposed finding. The presentation as a cancer-mimicking rectal mass is an unusual LGV manifestation, hence atypical. Red circle and electronic caliper measurements are visible annotations.
